correction: A bash helper that callers run in an if condition (if ! x="$(helper)") runs without set -e, so each jq or other step inside it must check its own status and the helper must reject a page that is not JSON or not an array; else a failed jq turns a bad page into a short, successful result and --apply writes on partial data
evidence: core#221 re-review 1 (openai/gpt-6.1-sol) of head 166f594, finding R1: paged_json returned page 1 only when page 2 was malformed JSON
